walkthroughs.body_html:
Sequences Functions & Graphs — a core area of GCSE Maths.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Sequences Functions & Graphs brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Sequences Functions & Graphs.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

options: 5n

mcqs.q: What is the difference between an arithmetic and a geometric sequence?
options: Arithmetic sequences involve only addition and geometric sequences only multiplication, so 1, 2, 4 is arithmetic.
Arithmetic has a constant difference between terms; geometric has a constant ratio.
It is reflected in the y-axis because of the minus.
Arithmetic sequences only use whole numbers and geometric sequences use decimals.

mcqs.q: How does the graph of y = f(x - 3) compare to y = f(x)?
options: It is reflected in the y-axis because of the minus.
It is translated 3 units to the right.
It is translated 3 units to the left because of the minus.
How long the line is on the page.

mcqs.q: What does the gradient of a straight-line graph tell you?
options: It is reflected in the y-axis because of the minus.
How steep the line is — the change in y for each unit change in x (rise over run).
How long the line is on the page.
Where the line crosses the y-axis.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Geometric sequence”?
options: Each term multiplied by a common ratio.
Formula giving any term from its position; e.g. 3n + 1 gives 4, 7, 10, …
Each term is the sum of the two before it (e.g. 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8).
Each number in a sequence.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Sequence”?
options: Each number in a sequence.
Each term multiplied by a common ratio.
Each term is the sum of the two before it (e.g. 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8).
List of numbers in a particular order following a rule.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Fibonacci-style”?
options: Common difference between consecutive terms. nth term: a + (n − 1)d.
Each term is the sum of the two before it (e.g. 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8).
List of numbers in a particular order following a rule.
Each term multiplied by a common ratio.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “nth term”?
options: Each number in a sequence.
Common difference between consecutive terms. nth term: a + (n − 1)d.
Each term multiplied by a common ratio.
Formula giving any term from its position; e.g. 3n + 1 gives 4, 7, 10, …

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Term”?
options: Each term is the sum of the two before it (e.g. 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8).
Formula giving any term from its position; e.g. 3n + 1 gives 4, 7, 10, …
Each number in a sequence.
Common difference between consecutive terms. nth term: a + (n − 1)d.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Arithmetic (linear) sequence”?
options: Formula giving any term from its position; e.g. 3n + 1 gives 4, 7, 10, …
Each term multiplied by a common ratio.
Each number in a sequence.
Common difference between consecutive terms. nth term: a + (n − 1)d.
